the effects of hypoxia and ischemia on the developing brain and the mechanisms of neuronal death.
how the developing brain is able to respond to oxygen deprivation, and the role of Na+ channels in these adaptations.

Na+ channel III is the predominant subtype regulated in response to hypoxia, and this regulation is dependent on age.

Na+ channel I is the major subtype expressed in the cortex during early postnatal development, and that Na+ channel III expression increases during prolonged hypoxia, while Na+ channel II expression is relatively unaffected by this condition.
Na+ channel I mRNA is down-regulated, Na+ channel II is unchanged and Na+ channel III mRNA is up-regulated by 5-day hypoxic exposure in the developing rat cerebral cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prolonged hypoxia up-regulates Na+ channel III mRNA expression in the immature cortex.

Na+ channel I expression is not affected by either hypoxic exposure or age, Na+ channel II expression is up-regualted with development and hypoxia has no effect, and Na+ channel III is up-regulated with development and hypoxic exposure.

Na+ channel III expression is up-regulate in response to prolonged oxygen deprivation.
